candidates.name: MAKE-BROADCAST-STREAM
candidates.law: Construct an output composite over ordered output streams; every output operation writes to every constituent in order; no constituents is valid and discards output.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Writing 'ab' through composite with two string outputs appends 'ab' to each.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Reject an input-only constituent as an output sink.

candidates.name: BROADCAST-STREAM-STREAMS
candidates.law: For a broadcast stream, return its ordered constituent output streams without copying their data or consuming output.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Constructor(s1,s2) exposes s1,s2 in constructor order.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return input streams or confuse this with writing output.

candidates.name: MAKE-ECHO-STREAM
candidates.law: Construct a bidirectional composite from an input stream and output stream; consumed input is echoed to output and explicit output is sent to output.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Reading character A from input causes A to appear in output; explicit B write also appears.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Echo does not manufacture a second copy of A on a mere unread operation.

candidates.name: ECHO-STREAM-INPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Return the exact input constituent of an echo stream, without consuming any input.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Echo(sin,sout) has input constituent sin.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Must not return sout or advance sin.

candidates.name: ECHO-STREAM-OUTPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Return the exact output constituent of an echo stream, without producing output.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Echo(sin,sout) has output constituent sout.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Must not return sin or write echoed input.

candidates.name: MAKE-TWO-WAY-STREAM
candidates.law: Build a bidirectional stream whose reads delegate to the designated input stream and writes delegate to the designated output stream; unlike an echo stream, reads need not echo.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Read X from input and write Y: output receives only Y.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Treat reading as an implicit echo or treat output sink as input.

candidates.name: TWO-WAY-STREAM-INPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Return the input constituent of a two-way stream without consuming it.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Two-way(sin,sout) yields sin.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Must not return sout.

candidates.name: TWO-WAY-STREAM-OUTPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Return the output constituent of a two-way stream without writing to it.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Two-way(sin,sout) yields sout.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Must not return sin.

candidates.name: MAKE-STRING-INPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Given string and optional bounding start,end indices, expose successive characters in [start,end), then EOF without reading outside range.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: The stream over 'abcde' bounds [1,4) yields b,c,d then EOF.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not read the excluded endpoints or accept indices outside the string.

candidates.name: MAKE-STRING-OUTPUT-STREAM
candidates.law: Create character output stream accumulating writes for later GET-OUTPUT-STREAM-STRING retrieval; initial buffer is empty.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Write A then B, extraction returns 'AB'.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Creation does not itself write characters and need not create a file.

candidates.name: LISTEN
candidates.law: Observe whether a character is immediately available from a character input stream without consuming it; EOF can return false.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Nonempty string input yields true and next READ-CHAR still sees the first character.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Never advance stream position or block waiting for unavailable future input.

candidates.name: PEEK-CHAR
candidates.law: Return the next matching input character without consuming it; optional peek-type may skip characters before the match and the specified EOF behavior applies.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: PEEK-CHAR nil before 'ab' yields a and following READ-CHAR yields a.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not consume the observed matched character.

candidates.name: READ-CHAR-NO-HANG
candidates.law: Attempt a character read only if immediately available; distinguish no available input from EOF, with optional EOF policy.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: For ready 'a' consumes and yields a; a temporarily unavailable stream yields NIL instead of waiting.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not report transient no-data as an actual EOF condition.

candidates.name: READ-LINE
candidates.law: Consume one line up to but not including newline and return text plus missing-newline flag; handle an EOF before any character under eof-error-p/eof-value policy.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Input 'a\nb' yields first line 'a' with missing-newline false, second 'b' with true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Never include terminating newline in the returned line text.

candidates.name: READ-SEQUENCE
candidates.law: Destructively fill specified sequence slice from stream elements; return the index of first element not updated when EOF intervenes.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Three-character input into a five-cell vector starting at index 1 updates three cells and returns index 4.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not overwrite sequence cells past end bound or assume full reads.

candidates.name: WRITE-SEQUENCE
candidates.law: Write successive elements from bounded sequence subsequence to output stream and return the sequence; preserve ordering and bounds.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Write [A,B,C] from [1,3) emits B,C.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not write elements before start or after end.

candidates.name: FRESH-LINE
candidates.law: Output newline only if output stream is not already at the beginning of a line; return whether newline was emitted.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: After writing 'x', FRESH-LINE emits a newline; calling again at line start emits none.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Never insert repeated blank lines at an existing line boundary.

candidates.name: CLEAR-INPUT
candidates.law: Discard input already available in the buffer of an input stream; do not promise to drain future input.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A buffered unread character may be discarded by CLEAR-INPUT.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not block until the physical input source closes.

candidates.name: CLEAR-OUTPUT
candidates.law: Try to abort pending, not-yet-transmitted output for a stream; already delivered data remains delivered.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Pending buffered data may be discarded while previously flushed data remains visible.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not claim bytes already sent to a device can be recalled.

candidates.name: FINISH-OUTPUT
candidates.law: Force pending output transmission and wait until it is completed as specified by the stream; unlike FORCE-OUTPUT it waits.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Buffered output is pushed and completion observed before returning.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not treat return before completion as FINISH-OUTPUT.

candidates.name: FORCE-OUTPUT
candidates.law: Initiate transmission of buffered output without promising completion before return; unlike FINISH-OUTPUT waiting is not required.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A pending buffer is scheduled for delivery.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not require full completion before returning or discard the pending buffer.

candidates.name: FILE-LENGTH
candidates.law: For a file stream, return length in stream elements, or NIL when it cannot be determined; do not confuse character count with encoded bytes.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A known 3-element binary file reports 3.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Character translations do not guarantee one-byte-per-character length.

candidates.name: FILE-POSITION
candidates.law: Without second argument observe current file position or NIL if unknown; with position designator attempt seek and return success predicate; preserve stream element units.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: For seekable file, save position p, read, seek back to p and reread same element.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Never assume character-stream positions increment one per character.

candidates.name: FILE-STRING-LENGTH
candidates.law: Return number of file position units output by writing given string or character to the designated character output file stream; result can depend on encoding.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: One ASCII character on one-byte external format has encoded file length 1.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not equate Unicode codepoint count to all external-format lengths.

candidates.name: STREAM-ELEMENT-TYPE
candidates.law: Report a type specifier for elements a stream can read/write; permitted representations need not be uniquely normalized.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Character stream element-type admits characters; binary stream admits relevant integers.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not require exact textual equality of equivalent type specifiers.

candidates.name: STREAM-EXTERNAL-FORMAT
candidates.law: For a file stream report the implementation's external format designator, whose representation may be implementation-specific.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Character file opened with selected external format reports a corresponding designator.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not claim the reported designator is portable to every Lisp runtime.

candidates.name: INPUT-STREAM-P
candidates.law: Return generalized true iff object is an input-capable stream, including bidirectional composites.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Make-string-input-stream object yields true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: An output-only string stream must not be reported input-capable.

candidates.name: OUTPUT-STREAM-P
candidates.law: Return generalized true iff object is an output-capable stream, including bidirectional composites.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Make-string-output-stream object yields true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: An input-only string stream must not be reported output-capable.

candidates.name: INTERACTIVE-STREAM-P
candidates.law: Return generalized true for an interactive stream designating a human interaction source or sink, false for ordinary noninteractive streams.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: An ordinary string input stream reports false.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not infer interactivity solely from input/output capability.

candidates.name: OPEN-STREAM-P
candidates.law: Report whether a stream is open; closing it changes this predicate without changing its identity.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: An open output stream yields true, after CLOSE yields false.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return true only because the stream object still exists.

candidates.name: STREAMP
candidates.law: Return generalized true exactly for stream objects, independent of current open/closed state.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A closed string stream remains a stream.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not test only open streams.

candidates.name: FILE-STREAM
candidates.law: Classify file-connected stream objects as file-stream class; do not treat an in-memory string stream as file-connected.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Stream obtained by opening a file is a file stream.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: An ordinary string-output-stream is not a file-stream.

candidates.name: END-OF-FILE
candidates.law: Represent the standard end-of-file condition signaled by a read with eof-error-p true at actual EOF; not a successful EOF value.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Reading past exhausted input with eof-error-p true signals END-OF-FILE.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: EOF-value return with eof-error-p false must not signal that condition.

candidates.name: MAKE-PATHNAME
candidates.law: Construct pathname from host/device/directory/name/type/version components and optional defaults, preserving unspecified components under documented merge/case rules.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Supplying name 'abc' and type 'lisp' produces pathname with matching NAME and TYPE.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not silently reinterpret explicit host or component case as a literal OS file open.

candidates.name: PARSE-NAMESTRING
candidates.law: Parse a bounded namestring into pathname and stopping index under host/default/junk-allowed rules, with filesystem-dependent component interpretation.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Parsing 'file.lisp' yields pathname designator plus consumed end index.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not claim a unique portable component representation for every host string.

candidates.name: PATHNAME
candidates.law: Coerce a pathname designator (pathname, string, file stream where allowed) to pathname object under implementation pathname syntax.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Applying PATHNAME to an existing pathname preserves pathname identity/equality.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not treat an arbitrary list as a pathname designator.

candidates.name: PATHNAMEP
candidates.law: Return generalized true exactly for pathname objects, irrespective of whether the named file exists.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: MAKE-PATHNAME result yields true without touching file system.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: A random string designating a file need not itself satisfy PATHNAMEP.

candidates.name: NAMESTRING
candidates.law: For a pathname represent its full pathname syntax as a namestring when a valid representation exists; result is subject to filesystem and host conventions.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A simple pathname on host supports a namestring that can be parsed on that host.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not treat pathname strings as universally identical across file systems.

candidates.name: HOST-NAMESTRING
candidates.law: Return the host-only namestring component for pathname without appending its directory, name or type.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A pathname with host H has host-only representation H under its host syntax.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return the entire original file namestring.

candidates.name: DIRECTORY-NAMESTRING
candidates.law: Return a namestring representing only pathname directory components, with host-specific syntax and NIL/unrepresentable outcomes.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Directory /tmp/part in pathname yields directory representation without leaf file name.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not include the filename/type component in DIRECTORY-NAMESTRING.

candidates.name: FILE-NAMESTRING
candidates.law: Return the file portion of pathname namestring (name, type and version as supported), excluding host/device/directory.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: For directory /tmp and leaf 'a.lisp', file namestring denotes 'a.lisp'.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return directory prefix.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-HOST
candidates.law: Extract pathname host component with optional :case normalization; host is not inferred to equal device.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: MAKE-PATHNAME with host H yields H under local case.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return full namestring in place of host.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-DEVICE
candidates.law: Extract pathname device component with optional :case normalization; may be :UNSPECIFIC when host has no device concept.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A pathname created with explicit device D reports D under suitable host.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not mistake directory for device.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-DIRECTORY
candidates.law: Extract structured pathname directory component (absolute/relative marker plus segments where applicable) under host case convention.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Pathname /a/b/c.lisp on Unix-like host reports absolute directory a,b.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return leaf filename or force Unix syntax on all hosts.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-NAME
candidates.law: Extract only pathname name component, not extension/type or directory, respecting :case.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: On appropriate host, 'a.lisp' yields name 'a'.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not include '.lisp' type in the name.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-TYPE
candidates.law: Extract pathname type component (extension-like but host-defined), respecting :case, distinguishing NIL/:UNSPECIFIC where relevant.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: On appropriate host, 'a.lisp' yields type 'lisp'.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not confuse empty string type with unspecified type.

candidates.name: PATHNAME-VERSION
candidates.law: Extract pathname version component where provided/supported; may be NIL or a special version keyword.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A pathname constructed with explicit version returns that version under its host conventions.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not conflate version with filename extension/type.

candidates.name: LOGICAL-PATHNAME
candidates.law: Coerce a valid logical pathname designator to a logical-pathname object using registered logical host syntax, not physical path resolution.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Valid logical host notation produces a logical pathname.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Unregistered logical host cannot silently become a physical pathname.

candidates.name: LOGICAL-PATHNAME-TRANSLATIONS
candidates.law: Read or set host-specific ordered translation patterns for logical pathname host; first applicable translation determines expansion.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Given an ordered translation table, translate-logical-pathname chooses first matching mapping.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not imply physical filesystem access when merely retrieving the table.

candidates.name: LOAD-LOGICAL-PATHNAME-TRANSLATIONS
candidates.law: Attempt to load translations for a named logical host, returning true if translations were loaded/available, or signal/return per specified host rules.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A configured logical host translation file enables subsequent logical resolution.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not report success when no host translations could be established.

candidates.name: HASHTABLE-COPY
candidates.law: R6RS HASHTABLE-COPY creates separate table with identical key-value associations and same key semantics; returned copy is immutable by default, mutable only when optional argument true.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Copy of table mapping a→1 maps a→1 but modifying original associations does not alter copy.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Default copy may not be treated as mutable; copying does not deep-copy each key/value.
archived_positive_claims: ["Copy of mutable {1↦one, 2↦two} with no second argument has both associations and hashtable-mutable? false; source stays mutable.","Copy with explicit true has hashtable-mutable? true; set! copy[1]=changed leaves original[1]=one."]
archived_negative_claims: ["A default copy accepts mutation or is reported mutable.","Mutating explicit-mutable copy changes an original association or losing mappings during copy."]

candidates.name: HASHTABLE-MUTABLE?
candidates.law: R6RS predicate returns true exactly when hashtable can be mutated through hash table updates, false for immutable copy.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Copy table without mutable flag yields false; copy with true flag yields true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not infer mutability from size or presence of key associations.
archived_positive_claims: ["Fresh make-eqv-hashtable is mutable.","Immutable default copy and explicit mutable copy have equal initial mappings, but mutability predicates return false versus true."]
archived_negative_claims: ["Result is inferred exclusively from hashtable contents or size, so equal-association mutable/immutable instances are indistinguishable.","A default immutable copy is reported mutable."]

candidates.name: CLASS-DIRECT-SUBCLASSES
candidates.law: CLOS MOP reader returns the class metaobjects whose direct superclasses include given class, excluding indirect descendants.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: If B directly inherits A and C inherits B, A's direct-subclasses includes B not C.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not include all transitive descendants.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-DIRECT-SUPERCLASSES
candidates.law: CLOS MOP reader yields direct superclass metaobjects of class in specified precedence; not entire transitive class precedence list.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Class C inheriting A and B directly returns [A,B].
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not append T unless it was a direct superclass.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-DEFAULT-INITARGS
candidates.law: For finalized class, return effective default initialization arguments computed from class precedence and inherited direct defaults; error on class not finalized.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Inherited superclass default initarg appears in finalized subclass effective list unless overridden.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return only direct defaults or claim valid access before finalization.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-DIRECT-DEFAULT-INITARGS
candidates.law: Return default initarg specifications declared directly by class, not inherited/effective defaults.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Class with no direct defaults yields empty list even if superclass declares one.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return merged inherited defaults.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-SLOTS
candidates.law: For finalized class, return effective slot-definition metaobjects after inheritance/class slot merging; distinguish from class-direct-slots.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Subclass with inherited and direct slots yields both among effective slots.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not exclude inherited slot definitions.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-FINALIZED-P
candidates.law: Return true iff class finalization has occurred; return false for uninitialized or forward-referenced class.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A nonfinalized class returns false; after FINALIZE-INHERITANCE it returns true.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not equate merely allocated class metaobject with finalized.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: CLASS-PROTOTYPE
candidates.law: For finalized class return representative prototype instance; initialization state unspecified, and portable clients must not mutate prototype slots.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Prototype is instance of target finalized class.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not require initialized slots or mutate prototype as a regular user object.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: GENERIC-FUNCTION-DECLARATIONS
candidates.law: CLOS MOP reader returns the declaration specifications associated with generic-function metaobject; does not inspect method bodies.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A generic function created with declarations returns corresponding declaration list.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not mistake per-method declarations for generic-function declarations.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: GENERIC-FUNCTION-LAMBDA-LIST
candidates.law: Return lambda-list associated with generic-function metaobject, not a particular method's differing implementation local parameter names.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A generic function requiring x,y has two required argument positions in its lambda list.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return one chosen method's specialized lambda list.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: GENERIC-FUNCTION-METHOD-CLASS
candidates.law: Return class metaobject designated to construct newly added method instances for generic function.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Generic function configured with method-class C reports C.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not confuse method class with class of the generic function itself.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: GENERIC-FUNCTION-METHOD-COMBINATION
candidates.law: Return method-combination metaobject associated with generic function; this controls method combination but is not method list.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A configured :around/:before combination property is represented by the returned combination object.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return set of methods instead of the combination metaobject.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: GENERIC-FUNCTION-NAME
candidates.law: Return name associated with generic-function metaobject, possibly NIL, independent of method names.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A named generic function's name reader returns its name.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not infer generic function name from a method qualifier.
archived_law_claims: Read specified metaobject state only; distinctness from already-selected D10 and source implementation representation NOT proved.

candidates.name: COS
candidates.law: Compute cosine of numeric argument in radians; for complex inputs use analytic complex cosine; floating accuracy remains implementation-specific.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: COS(0)=1 up to permitted numeric type/precision.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not treat numeric argument as degrees by default.

candidates.name: RANDOM
candidates.law: Generate pseudo-random value below positive bound n from random-state: for positive integer n result is integer in [0,n); for positive float bound result is nonnegative float below bound.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: RANDOM(5) always yields integer among 0..4 under a valid state.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not return bound itself or treat successive results as a deterministic pure function of n alone.

candidates.name: FLOATP
candidates.law: Historical floating-point type predicate tests representation category (float), not integrality of mathematical value.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A float 1.0 satisfies FLOATP even when numerical value equals integer 1.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: An exact integer 1 must not satisfy FLOATP.
archived_law_claims: fixed/floating and logical-word observations tied to machine carrier

candidates.name: FIXP
candidates.law: Historical FIXP tests whether object is implemented as machine fixed integer under donor implementation, not any arbitrary-precision integer.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: A machine fixnum 3 yields true in a runtime supporting that historical type.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: A bignum exceeding fixnum range does not satisfy FIXP even though NUMBERP may hold.
archived_law_claims: fixed/floating and logical-word observations tied to machine carrier

candidates.name: LEFTSHIFT
candidates.law: On historical nonnegative finite machine integer x and nonnegative shift count n, shift bits left by n inserting zeros; overflow handling depends on donor word width.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: Unsigned binary 0011 shifted left by 2 becomes 1100 where width permits.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not assume infinite precision if historical machine word overflow semantics apply.
archived_law_claims: fixed/floating and logical-word observations tied to machine carrier

candidates.name: LOGOR
candidates.law: Bitwise inclusive OR on integer bit representations; a result bit is 1 iff at least one operand corresponding bit is 1, with donor sign-width conventions.
candidates.positive_illustrative_claim: 0101 LOGOR 0011 is 0111 at fixed 4-bit nonnegative width.
candidates.negative_illustrative_claim: Do not apply logical short-circuit boolean OR to entire integer words.
archived_law_claims: fixed/floating and logical-word observations tied to machine carrier
